summary: Portfolio is riding a powerful AI/space momentum wave, but three positions (RKLB, QQQ, APLD) sit above your 15% single-name comfort line and the high-beta sleeve (RKLB, APLD, IREN, ONDS) dominates risk. RKLB in particular is parabolic with RSI 78 and annualized vol of 89% — this is a balanced-risk portfolio in name only right now. The right move is disciplined trimming into strength, not chasing.

insights.headline: Parabolic move, 30% weight, RSI 78 — trim into strength
insights.detail: Up 254% in 6m, 91% in 1m, beta 2.31, vol 89%, RSI 78. News flow is SpaceX-IPO-hype and short-squeeze driven, not fundamentals. P/E undefined, $87B cap on a still-pre-profit launcher. At 30% of the book, a single bad earnings or share sale (see Firefly precedent in headlines) wipes out a material chunk of net worth.

suggested_action.thesis: This is a risk-management trade, not a thesis change. RKLB has tripled in six months, RSI is deeply overbought, and 30% in a beta-2.3 story stock is incompatible with a balanced profile. Lock in some of the +70% gain and bring the position back inside your stated 15% ceiling.
suggested_action.catalyst: Mean reversion after SpaceX IPO hype fades; any secondary offering or Neutron timeline slip; broad risk-off in high-beta names.
suggested_action.risks: Momentum continues and you underweight a winner. Mitigated by keeping a still-meaningful 12–15% stake — you stay long the story, just not levered to it.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Balanced risk + medium horizon + 15% cap explicitly calls for trimming a 30% high-vol single name.

insights.headline: Core exposure but oversized at 25%
insights.detail: QQQ at 25.3% on top of VOO 10.4% means ~36% in broad US large-cap beta, heavily tech-tilted. RSI 70, above both MAs — healthy uptrend, not a sell, but the weight exceeds your stated 15% comfort line for a single ticker.

suggested_action.thesis: QQQ is a fine core holding, but it overlaps heavily with VOO and pushes your tech beta even higher when you already own APLD, IREN, ONDS. Right-sizing toward 15% reduces redundancy without changing portfolio character.
suggested_action.catalyst: Use any continued melt-up to rebalance; no urgency.
suggested_action.risks: Tech keeps leading and you give up some upside. Minor — VOO captures most of it.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Respects the 15% single-position ceiling while keeping diversified equity beta intact.

insights.headline: Hyperscaler lease is real, but beta 5.7 and 18% weight is too much
insights.detail: 15-year hyperscaler lease materially de-risks the AI campus build-out and the stock has confirmed it (+52% 1m, +106% 6m). But beta 5.7 and annualized vol 114% mean this is the single most explosive name in the book, and it's above your 15% cap.

suggested_action.thesis: The fundamental story improved meaningfully with the hyperscaler lease, so don't exit — but a 5.7-beta name has no business being 18% of a balanced portfolio. Take it to ~12–14%.
suggested_action.catalyst: Next lease announcement or financing update could spike or sink it; either way, you want to be inside your size limit before that print.
suggested_action.risks: AI capex narrative cools, financing dilution, or a single tenant concentration scare. All amplified by the vol profile.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Keeps meaningful exposure to a working thesis while honoring the 15% rule on a high-vol name.

insights.headline: True core — leave alone, likely add with trim proceeds
insights.detail: Vol 12%, broad diversification, 1.08% yield, steady +13% over 6m. Only 10.4% of book — under-weighted relative to the speculative sleeve.

suggested_action.thesis: Use proceeds from RKLB/APLD/QQQ trims to lift VOO. It's the lowest-vol, most-diversified piece of the book and currently under-represented versus the high-beta sleeve.
suggested_action.risks: Broad market drawdown hits VOO too, but by definition less than the rest of the portfolio.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Balanced profile demands a larger ballast against the high-beta names you're keeping.

insights.headline: Nvidia Blackwell deal is a legit catalyst; size is appropriate
insights.detail: $1.6B Nvidia infrastructure deal and ARR raised to $4.4B are concrete, not hype. Beta 4.18 and vol 101% are extreme, but at 9.3% weight the sizing is finally sensible for a name like this. RSI 56 — not stretched.

suggested_action.thesis: Fundamental story is upgrading and the position is correctly sized. No reason to touch it.
suggested_action.catalyst: Further hyperscaler / GPU-cloud contract announcements, quarterly ARR updates.
suggested_action.risks: AI infrastructure capex cycle peaks; bitcoin mining legacy exposure remains; financing/dilution risk at 88x P/E.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: High-beta name kept under the 15% ceiling — exactly how a balanced investor should hold these.

insights.headline: Only laggard in the book, but below both MAs
insights.detail: -11.9% / -15.3% / -41% trailing returns, below 50d and 200d MAs, RSI 49. Tech-platform revenue and stablecoin launch are interesting optionality but not yet showing in the tape. Position is small (4.8%) so it's not hurting much.

suggested_action.thesis: Don't add to a downtrend. Wait for price to reclaim the 50-day and for tech-platform revenue to show up in earnings before sizing up. Don't sell a small position into weakness without a thesis break either.
suggested_action.catalyst: Next earnings print — specifically tech-platform segment growth; reclaim of 50d MA.
suggested_action.risks: Consumer credit deterioration, stablecoin/regulatory noise distracting from core lending economics.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Small speculative fintech exposure is fine for a balanced investor; just don't average down blindly.

insights.headline: Tiny speculative drone bet — fine as-is
insights.detail: 1.8% weight, +73% unrealized, vol 125%, P/E 120. Pure thematic drone/defense lottery ticket. Too small to matter to portfolio outcomes, large enough to participate if the theme runs.

insights.headline: 30 bps stub position — clean up or commit
insights.detail: 0.3% of portfolio (~$7). Below both MAs, RSI 29 (oversold), 6m -27.5%. At this size it's noise; the only question is whether you have conviction to make it meaningful.

suggested_action.thesis: A 0.3% position cannot move the needle either way. Either size up to a real position (2–4%) with a documented thesis on vonoprazan exclusivity and 2026 profitability, or close it and free the mental overhead. Given the downtrend and your indifference to the story, closing is the cleaner call.
suggested_action.risks: PHAT rips on a profitability beat after you sell. Cost of being wrong: trivial given size.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Balanced investors don't carry sub-1% stub positions; either conviction or exit.

concentration_flags: RKLB at 30% is 2x your stated 15% single-name ceiling and is the highest-vol name in the book — this is the single biggest risk in the portfolio.
QQQ at 25% exceeds the 15% ceiling and overlaps heavily with VOO, compounding US large-cap tech beta.
APLD at 18% exceeds the ceiling on a beta-5.7, 114%-vol name — sizing is inconsistent with a balanced profile.
Aggregate high-beta sleeve (RKLB + APLD + IREN + ONDS) ≈ 59% of the book; effective portfolio beta is well above 'balanced.'
